\chapter{Chapter08 — Generalized Fourier Formulas}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter08.GeneralizedFourierFormulas}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Zero multi-index]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.zeroMultiIndex}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b004}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.zeroMultiIndex}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.MultiIndex}
Given a finite Fourier basis $B$ and a natural number $n$, the zero multi-index is the
$n$-coordinate multi-index whose every entry is the distinguished index of the
constant-one basis vector.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Mean under a product distribution]
\lean{FABL.productMean}
\label{FABL.productMean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productProbabilityPMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite type, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$n$ be a natural number, and let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega)\to\mathbb{R}$. The
product mean of $f$ is its expectation when the $n$ coordinates are sampled
independently according to $\pi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Second moment under a product distribution]
\lean{FABL.productSecondMoment}
\label{FABL.productSecondMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productProbabilityPMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite type, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$n$ be a natural number, and let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega)\to\mathbb{R}$. The
product second moment of $f$ is the expectation of $f(x)^2$ when the $n$ coordinates of
$x$ are sampled independently according to $\pi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Variance on a product space]
\lean{FABL.productVariance}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b001
}
\label{FABL.productVariance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productMean, FABL.productProbabilityPMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. Its variance under the product probability
distribution $\pi^{\otimes n}$ is the expected squared deviation from its mean: $\mathbb
E_{x\sim\pi^{\otimes n}}[(f(x)-\mathbb E_{y\sim\pi^{\otimes n}}f(y))^2]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Covariance on a product space]
\lean{FABL.productCovariance}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b005
}
\label{FABL.productCovariance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productMean, FABL.productProbabilityPMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, and let $f,g:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. Their covariance under the product
probability distribution $\pi^{\otimes n}$ is $\mathbb E_{x\sim\pi^{\otimes
n}}[(f(x)-\mathbb E_{u\sim\pi^{\otimes n}}f(u))(g(x)-\mathbb E_{v\sim\pi^{\otimes
n}}g(v))]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Negation of a probability expectation]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_neg_general}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_neg_general}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. The expectation of $-f$ under $\pi$ equals the negative of
the expectation of $f$ under $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linearity of expectation under subtraction]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_sub_general}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_sub_general}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_neg_general}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. Then
$\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[f-g]=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[f]-\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[g]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of expectation for functions]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_add_fun}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_add_fun}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then the expectation of their pointwise sum is the sum of
their expectations: $\mathbb E_\pi(f+g)=\mathbb E_\pi f+\mathbb E_\pi g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling a finite expectation]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_smul_fun}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_smul_fun}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$c\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. The expectation of the pointwise
scalar multiple $cf$ under $\pi$ equals $c$ times the expectation of $f$ under $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_add}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_add}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For
any nonnegative integer $n$, functions $f,g:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and product Fourier
index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient of $f+g$ at $a$ is the sum of the Fourier
coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling of Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_smul}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a
finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by
$\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For every
real scalar $c$, function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, and multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the
Fourier coefficient of $cf$ at $a$ is $c$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients of a difference]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_sub}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_sub}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_add, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_smul, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a
finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by
$\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For
functions $f,g:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$ and a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier
coefficient of $f-g$ at $a$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ minus the Fourier
coefficient of $g$ at $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of the zero function]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zero}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_const}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of the
real-valued functions on $\Omega$, indexed by $\iota$, whose zero-indexed vector is
constant one and whose vectors are orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$.
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier
coefficient of the zero function on $\Omega^n$ at $a$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients of product basis functions]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productFunction}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction_orthonormal, FABL.MultiIndex}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a
finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by
$\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For
multi-indices $a,b\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient at $a$ of the product of basis
functions indexed coordinatewise by $b$ is $1$ if $a=b$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of a piecewise function]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_ite}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_ite}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2}
\difficulty{4}
Let $Ω$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $π$, and let $ι$ be a finite
nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions on $Ω$ that is
orthonormal for the $π$-weighted inner product and has a distinguished index $0_B$ whose
basis function is constantly one. For every $n\ge 0$, proposition $P$, functions
$f,g:Ω^n\to\mathbb R$, and multi-index $a\inι^n$, the Fourier coefficient at $a$ of the
function equal to $f$ when $P$ holds and to $g$ otherwise equals the corresponding
piecewise choice between the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$.
\end{theorem}

  {context}

\proofstep
  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p013-b007}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite Fourier basis on $\Omega$ indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$. For any
two functions $f,g:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, their inner product under the product
probability measure equals the sum of the products of their Fourier coefficients:
$\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{a\in\iota^n}\widehat f(a)\widehat g(a)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variance and squared Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.variance_eq_sum_sq_fourierCoeff}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b002
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.variance_eq_sum_sq_fourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_centered, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.parseval, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.zeroMultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productMean, FABL.productSecondMoment, FABL.productVariance}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$, with one basis vector equal to the constant-one function and with the basis
orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$. For every natural number $n$ and every function
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, the variance of $f$ under the product probability measure
equals the sum of the squares of its Fourier coefficients over all multi-indices except
the constant multi-index.
\end{theorem}

Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For
any nonnegative integer $n$ and functions $f,g:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, their covariance
under the product measure $\pi^n$ equals $\sum_{a\ne(0,\ldots,0)}\widehat f(a)\widehat
g(a)$, where the hats denote product Fourier coefficients.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Merge two coordinate vectors]
\lean{FABL.mergeOnCoordinates}
\label{FABL.mergeOnCoordinates}
\leanok
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and let
$x,y:\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega$. Their merge along $J$ is the vector equal to $x$ on
coordinates in $J$ and equal to $y$ on all other coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Dependence on a coordinate set]
\lean{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p044-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p212-b002
}
\label{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2}
Let $\Omega$ be a set, let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and
let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The function $f$ depends only on the coordinates in $J$
if, whenever $x,y\in\Omega^n$ agree at every coordinate in $J$, one has $f(x)=f(y)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Projection onto a coordinate set]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p212-b002
}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.mergeOnCoordinates, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productProbabilityPMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. For
$x\in\Omega^n$, define its projection onto functions of the coordinates in $J$ by
averaging $f$ over an independent product-distributed input $y$, while retaining $x$ on
$J$: $P_Jf(x)=\mathbb E_{y\sim\pi^{\otimes n}} f(z)$, where $z_i=x_i$ for $i\in J$ and
$z_i=y_i$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_add}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $f,g:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The
coordinate projection that keeps the input coordinates in $J$ and averages over the
remaining coordinates with respect to the product distribution induced by $\pi$
satisfies $P_J(f+g)=P_Jf+P_Jg$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_smul}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $c\in\mathbb{R}$, and let
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$. Then the coordinate projection satisfies $P_J(cf)=cP_Jf$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-sum preservation by coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_sum}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.mergeOnCoordinates, FABL.pmfExpectation_sum, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ and $\kappa$ be finite sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For any
family of functions $f_k:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ indexed by $k\in\kappa$, the coordinate
projection satisfies $P_J\bigl(\sum_{k\in\kappa}f_k\bigr)=\sum_{k\in\kappa}P_Jf_k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate dependence of the projection]

\proofstep
  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, and let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For every function
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, its coordinate projection $P_Jf$, obtained by keeping the
coordinates in $J$ and averaging over the others under the product distribution induced
by $\pi$, depends only on the coordinates in $J$: whenever $x_i=y_i$ for all $i\in J$,
one has $(P_Jf)(x)=(P_Jf)(y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Projection fixes coordinate-dependent functions]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_eq_self_of_dependsOnly}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_eq_self_of_dependsOnly}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.mergeOnCoordinates, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, and let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. If $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ depends only
on the coordinates in $J$, then its coordinate projection $P_Jf$, formed by averaging
over the other coordinates under the product distribution induced by $\pi$, equals $f$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with $\phi_0$ the constant function $1$. For every
basis index $a$, the expectation of $\phi_a$ under $\pi$ is $1$ if $a=0$ and $0$
otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Support contained in a set]
\lean{FABL.multiIndexSupport_subset_iff}
\label{FABL.multiIndexSupport_subset_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.multiIndexSupport}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\iota$ be a type with decidable equality, choose
$z\in\iota$, and let $a:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\iota$. For any set $J$ of positions, every
position $i$ with $a(i)\ne z$ belongs to $J$ if and only if $a(i)=z$ for every position
$i$ outside $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate projection of a product basis function]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.projectOnCoordinates_productFunction}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.projectOnCoordinates_productFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.expect_basis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.mergeOnCoordinates, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.multiIndexSupport_subset_iff, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_independentProductPMF_prod, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose
constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted
inner product. For a positive integer $n$, a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, and a set of
coordinates $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the projection of the product basis function
indexed by $a$ onto $J$ equals that product basis function if every coordinate where $a$
is not indexed by $0$ belongs to $J$, and equals zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set with decidable equality. Suppose $B$ is a basis
of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function at an index
$0_B$ and is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, a set of
coordinates $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and
$x\in\Omega^n$, the expectation of $f$ after replacing the coordinates in $J$ of an
independent sample from $\pi^n$ by those of $x$ is
$\sum_{a:\,\operatorname{supp}(a)\subseteq J}\widehat f(a)\,\psi_a(x)$, where
$\operatorname{supp}(a)=\{i:a_i\ne 0_B\}$, $\widehat
f(a)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi^n}[f(y)\psi_a(y)]$, and
$\psi_a(x)=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}B_{a_i}(x_i)$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a
finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by
$\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For a
subset $J$ of the $n$ coordinates, define the coordinate projection by fixing the
coordinates in $J$ and averaging over an independent product sample from $\pi$ in the
other coordinates. For a function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$ and multi-index
$a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient of this projection at $a$ equals the coefficient
of $f$ at $a$ if every coordinate where $a$ differs from the constant index belongs to
$J$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Idempotence of coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_idempotent}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_idempotent}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_injective, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_projectOnCoordinates, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and suppose
there is a finite nonempty index set $\iota$ and a basis of the real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner
product weighted by $\pi$. For any natural number $n$, any $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
and any $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, applying the coordinate projection onto $J$ twice
gives the same function as applying it once: $P_J(P_Jf)=P_Jf$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-adjointness of coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_selfAdjoint}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_selfAdjoint}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_projectOnCoordinates, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.plancherel, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInner, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and suppose
there is a finite nonempty index set $\iota$ and a basis of the real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner
product weighted by $\pi$. For any natural number $n$, any $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
and any functions $f,g:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, the product inner product weighted by the
product distribution induced by $\pi$ satisfies $\langle f,P_Jg\rangle=\langle
P_Jf,g\rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing coefficient outside the dependence set]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_of_dependsOnly}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b003
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_of_dependsOnly}
\leanok

\proofstep
  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $Ω$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $π$, and let $ι$ be a finite
nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions on $Ω$ that is
orthonormal for the $π$-weighted inner product and has a distinguished index $0_B$ whose
basis function is constantly one. For $n\ge 0$, let $J$ be a set of coordinates and let
$f:Ω^n\to\mathbb R$ depend only on the coordinates in $J$, meaning that inputs agreeing
on $J$ have the same value under $f$. If a multi-index $a\inι^n$ has a nonconstant
coordinate outside $J$, then the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Projection omitting one coordinate]
\lean{FABL.coordinateProjection}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005
}
\label{FABL.coordinateProjection}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. The coordinate
projection of $f$ at $i$ is its projection onto all coordinates other than $i$, obtained
by averaging over the product distribution while retaining the input on those other
coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Support contained in a punctured set]
\lean{FABL.multiIndexSupport_subset_erase_iff}
\label{FABL.multiIndexSupport_subset_erase_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.multiIndexSupport_subset_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\iota$ be a type with decidable equality, choose
$z\in\iota$, and let $a:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\iota$. For any position $i$, the set of
positions $j$ for which $a(j)\ne z$ is contained in all positions except $i$ if and only
if $a(i)=z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier expansion of a coordinate average]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.coordinateProjection_fourier_expansion}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b012
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.coordinateProjection_fourier_expansion}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.projectOnCoordinates_fourier_expansion, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.multiIndexSupport_subset_erase_iff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For
any nonnegative integer $n$, coordinate $i$, function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and
point $x\in\Omega^n$, the average of $f$ over coordinate $i$ while holding all other
coordinates fixed equals $\sum_{a:a_i=0}\widehat f(a)\prod_{j=1}^n\phi_{a_j}(x_j)$,
where $\widehat f(a)$ denotes the product Fourier coefficient of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate difference operator]
\lean{FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p049-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005
}
\label{FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. The coordinate
difference operator at $i$ sends $f$ to the function $x\mapsto f(x)-P_{-i}f(x)$, where
$P_{-i}f$ is the average of $f$ over the product distribution with all coordinates other
than $i$ fixed at their values in $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of the coordinate Laplacian]
\lean{FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian_add}
\label{FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.projectOnCoordinates_add}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
consider real-valued functions on $\Omega^n$. For every coordinate $i$, the product
coordinate Laplacian is additive: its value on $f+g$ is the sum of its values on $f$ and
$g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of the coordinate Laplacian]
\lean{FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian_smul}
\label{FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.projectOnCoordinates_smul}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. For every coordinate $i$ and scalar $c\in\mathbb R$, the
product coordinate Laplacian of $cf$ is $c$ times the product coordinate Laplacian of
$f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Influence of a coordinate]
\lean{FABL.productInfluence}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p002-b002,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p011-b006
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005
}
\label{FABL.productInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.productInner}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The influence of
coordinate $i$ on $f$ is the product-space inner product of the coordinate difference
$f-P_{-i}f$ with itself.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Total influence]
\lean{FABL.productTotalInfluence}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p011-b006}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p049-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005
}
\label{FABL.productTotalInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInfluence}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. The total influence of $f$ is the sum, over
all coordinates, of their individual influences on $f$.
\end{definition}

  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $Ω$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $π$, and let $ι$ be a finite
nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions on $Ω$ that is
orthonormal for the $π$-weighted inner product and has a distinguished index $0_B$ whose
basis function is constantly one. For any $n\ge 0$, coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
function $f:Ω^n\to\mathbb R$, and multi-index $a\inι^n$, the Fourier coefficient of the
function obtained by averaging $f$ over all coordinates other than $i$ is the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $a$ if $a_i=0_B$, and is zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite Fourier basis on $\Omega$ indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$, with
distinguished constant basis index $0_B$. For any coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, and point $x\in\Omega^n$, the product coordinate
Laplacian of $f$ at $x$ is $\sum_{a\in\iota^n:\,a_i\ne 0_B}\widehat f(a)\prod_{j=1}^n
B_{a_j}(x_j)$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on
$\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$
that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the constant-one
function. For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and
every coordinate $i$, the influence of $f$ at $i$ equals the sum of the squares of its
Fourier coefficients over all index tuples whose entry at coordinate $i$ is not the
distinguished constant-function index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Multi-index order as an indicator sum]
\lean{FABL.multiIndexOrder_cast_eq_sum_indicator}
\label{FABL.multiIndexOrder_cast_eq_sum_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.multiIndexOrder}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\iota$ be a type with decidable equality, choose a
distinguished element $z\in\iota$, and let $a:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\iota$. The number of
positions $i$ for which $a(i)\ne z$, viewed as a real number, equals
$\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\mathbf{1}_{a(i)\ne z}$.
\end{theorem}

Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
a finite nonempty index set carry an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on
$\mathcal{X}$ that includes the constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates
and function $f$ on $\mathcal{X}^n$, its total influence equals the sum, over all index
tuples $a$, of $\mathrm{ord}(a)\widehat f(a)^2$, where $\mathrm{ord}(a)$ counts the
coordinates at which $a$ is not the distinguished constant index and $\widehat f(a)$ is
the corresponding Fourier coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of product influence]
\lean{FABL.productInfluence_nonneg}
\label{FABL.productInfluence_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfInner_self_nonneg, FABL.productInfluence}
\difficulty{1}
For a finite set $\Omega$, a probability distribution $\pi$ on $\Omega$, a nonnegative
integer $n$, a real-valued function on $\Omega^n$, and any coordinate
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the influence at coordinate $i$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Projection and coordinate Laplacian sum]
\lean{FABL.coordinateProjection_add_laplacian}
\label{FABL.coordinateProjection_add_laplacian}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a
nonnegative integer, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. The
coordinate projection of $f$ onto all coordinates except $i$, plus the coordinate
Laplacian of $f$ at $i$, equals $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate projection decomposition]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productInner_eq_projection_add_laplacian}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productInner_eq_projection_add_laplacian}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_coordinateProjection, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.plancherel, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.productInner}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set labeling an orthonormal basis of real functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function. For a positive integer $n$, equip
functions on $\Omega^n$ with the product probability inner product. For each coordinate
$i$, let $P_i f$ be the average of $f$ over that coordinate with all other coordinates
fixed, and set $L_i f=f-P_i f$. Then for all such functions $f,g$,
\[
\langle f,g\rangle=\langle P_i f,P_i g\rangle+\langle L_i f,L_i g\rangle.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Replace one coordinate]
\lean{FABL.replaceCoordinate}
\label{FABL.replaceCoordinate}
\leanok
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $x:\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega$, let
$i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and let $\omega\in\Omega$. Replacing coordinate $i$ of $x$ by
$\omega$ gives the vector whose value at $i$ is $\omega$ and whose other coordinates
agree with $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate projection apply]
\lean{FABL.coordinateProjection_apply}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p212-b002}
\label{FABL.coordinateProjection_apply}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate conditional variance]
\lean{FABL.coordinateConditionalVariance}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p062-b011,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b002
}
\label{FABL.coordinateConditionalVariance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let
$f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and choose a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and an
input $x\in\Omega^n$. The conditional variance of $f$ when coordinate $i$ is resampled
from $\pi$, with the other coordinates fixed at $x$, is the $\pi$-expectation of the
squared deviation from the corresponding conditional mean.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Functions with sign range]
\lean{FABL.HasSignRange}
\label{FABL.HasSignRange}
\leanok
Let $\Omega$ be a type and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. The function has sign range if
every value of $f$ is either $-1$ or $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of a sign-valued function]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_mem_Icc_of_hasSignRange}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_mem_Icc_of_hasSignRange}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$. Then the expectation of $f$ under $\pi$ lies in the interval
$[-1,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment of a sign-valued function]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_sq_eq_one_of_hasSignRange}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_sq_eq_one_of_hasSignRange}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. The expectation of $f^2$
under $\pi$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$. Then the expected absolute deviation from the mean equals the
expected squared deviation from the mean:
\[\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}\bigl[|f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}f(y)|\bigr]=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}\bigl[(f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}f(y))^2\bigr].\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign disagreement and variance]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_independent_disagreement_eq_half_variance}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_independent_disagreement_eq_half_variance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add_fun, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_smul_fun, FABL.pmfExpectation_sq_eq_one_of_hasSignRange}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$. If $X$ and $Y$ are independent samples from $\pi$, then
$\mathbb{P}(f(X)\ne
f(Y))=\frac12\mathbb{E}_{X\sim\pi}\bigl[(f(X)-\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim\pi}f(Z))^2\bigr]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Projection is invariant under replacing the projected coordinate]
\lean{FABL.coordinateProjection_replaceCoordinate}
\label{FABL.coordinateProjection_replaceCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.projectOnCoordinates_dependsOnly, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a
nonnegative integer, let $i$ be a coordinate, let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and let
$x\in\Omega^n$ and $\omega\in\Omega$. The projection of $f$ onto all coordinates except
$i$ has the same value at $x$ and at the point obtained by replacing coordinate $i$ of
$x$ with $\omega$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean preservation by coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productMean_projectOnCoordinates}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productMean_projectOnCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_projectOnCoordinates, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zeroMultiIndex, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.zeroMultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.productMean, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the
constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, any subset $J$ of the
coordinates, and any function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, the product mean of the
projection of $f$ onto the coordinates in $J$ equals the product mean of $f$.
\end{theorem}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on
$\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$
that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the constant-one
function. For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and
every coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the influence of $f$ at $i$ equals the
product-distribution expectation of its conditional variance when only coordinate $i$ is
resampled from $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Mean absolute coordinate Laplacian]
\lean{FABL.productLaplacianL1}
\label{FABL.productLaplacianL1}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.productMean}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite type, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$n$ be a natural number, let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega)\to\mathbb{R}$, and let
$i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. The product Laplacian $L^1$ quantity at coordinate $i$ is the
product mean of the absolute value of the coordinate Laplacian of $f$ at $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Projected absolute Laplacian and conditional variance]
\lean{FABL.coordinateProjection_abs_laplacian_eq_coordinateConditionalVariance}
\label{FABL.coordinateProjection_abs_laplacian_eq_coordinateConditionalVariance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateConditionalVariance, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.coordinateProjection_apply, FABL.coordinateProjection_replaceCoordinate, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_eq_variance_of_hasSignRange, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a
nonnegative integer, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$.
For each coordinate $i$, projecting the pointwise absolute value of the coordinate
Laplacian of $f$ onto all coordinates except $i$ gives the conditional variance of $f$
in coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate resampling disagreement probability]
\lean{FABL.coordinateResamplingDisagreementProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p062-b011,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b002
}
\label{FABL.coordinateResamplingDisagreementProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productMean, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let
$f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and choose a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Draw an
input $x$ from the product distribution with marginal $\pi$, then independently resample
coordinate $i$ from $\pi$ while keeping the other coordinates fixed. The coordinate
resampling disagreement probability is the probability that the two resulting values of
$f$ differ.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Resampling disagreement and conditional variance]
\lean{FABL.coordinateProjection_resamplingDisagreement_eq_half_variance}
\label{FABL.coordinateProjection_resamplingDisagreement_eq_half_variance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateConditionalVariance, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.coordinateProjection_apply, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_independent_disagreement_eq_half_variance, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a
nonnegative integer, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$.
For each coordinate $i$, project onto all coordinates except $i$ the function that, at
each input, is the $\pi$-probability that resampling coordinate $i$ changes the value of
$f$. The resulting function equals one half of the conditional variance of $f$ in
coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of the product mean]
\lean{FABL.productMean_smul}
\label{FABL.productMean_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.productMean}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$,
and let $n$ be a natural number. For every real number $c$ and real-valued function
$f$ on $\Omega^n$, the product mean of $cf$ is $c$ times the product mean of $f$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on
$\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$
that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the constant-one
function. For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ taking
only the values $-1$ and $1$, and every coordinate $i$, the influence of $f$ at $i$
equals twice the probability that replacing coordinate $i$ by an independent sample from
$\pi$ changes the value of $f$, with the original input drawn from the product
distribution $\pi^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Spectral product noise operator]
\lean{FABL.spectralProductNoiseOperator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b007
}
\label{FABL.spectralProductNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexOrder}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ for
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$. Suppose one
basis vector, indexed by $a_0$, is the constant-one function. For
$f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$, its spectral product noise
transform at $x\in\Omega^n$ is the sum over product-basis indices $a\in\iota^n$ of the
Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ times the product-basis function at $x$, weighted by
$\rho^{|a|}$, where $|a|$ counts the coordinates of $a$ that differ from $a_0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Single-coordinate product noise operator]
\lean{FABL.productSingleCoordinateNoiseOperator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p063-b014}
\label{FABL.productSingleCoordinateNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let
$f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and choose a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and a real
parameter $\rho$. The single-coordinate product noise transform of $f$ is the sum of its
projection onto functions independent of coordinate $i$ and $\rho$ times its
product-coordinate Laplacian in coordinate $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient under single-coordinate noise]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productSingleCoordinateNoiseOperator}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productSingleCoordinateNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_add, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_coordinateProjection, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_smul, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productSingleCoordinateNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite
nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by $\iota$
under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For any
coordinate $i$ among the $n$ coordinates, any real $\rho$, any function
$f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, and any multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient
of the single-coordinate noise operator applied to $f$ at $a$ is the Fourier coefficient
of $f$ at $a$ multiplied by $1$ if $a_i$ is the constant index, and by $\rho$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $\pi$. Suppose a
finite nonempty index set $\iota$ indexes a basis of the real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the
constant-one function as one basis vector. For every $n\ge 0$, coordinate
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, real parameters $\rho,\sigma$, and function
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, applying the single-coordinate noise operator with parameter
$\sigma$ and then with parameter $\rho$ gives the same function as applying it once with
parameter $\rho\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Anisotropic product noise operator]
\lean{FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p064-b001}
\label{FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.ProductL2}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ for
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$. Suppose one
basis vector, indexed by $a_0$, is the constant-one function. Given a function
$f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and real coordinate parameters $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_n$,
its anisotropic product noise transform at $x\in\Omega^n$ is the sum over product-basis
indices $a\in\iota^n$ of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ times the product-basis
function at $x$, weighted by the product of $\rho_j$ over coordinates $j$ for which
$a_j\ne a_0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients under anisotropic product noise]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourier_expansion_unique, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set with decidable equality. Let $B$ be a basis of
real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner
product, with a distinguished index $0_B$ whose basis function is constantly one. For
any nonnegative integer $n$, coordinate parameters $\rho_i\in\mathbb R$ for
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, function $f:(\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$, and
multi-index $a:\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\iota$, the Fourier coefficient of the anisotropic
product noise transform of $f$ at $a$ equals $\left(\prod_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}\ n}
w_i\right)$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$, where $w_i=1$ if $a(i)=0_B$ and
$w_i=\rho_i$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Constant-parameter product noise operator]
\lean{FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator_const}
\label{FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator_const}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_injective, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourier_expansion_unique, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator, FABL.multiIndexOrder, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.spectralProductNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$, indexed by $\iota$, whose distinguished basis vector is constant $1$ and
whose vectors are orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For any natural
number $n$, real parameter $\rho$, and real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, the
anisotropic product noise operator with parameter equal to $\rho$ in every coordinate
agrees with the spectral product noise operator with parameter $\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Single-coordinate product noise]
\lean{FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator_single}
\label{FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator_single}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_injective, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productSingleCoordinateNoiseOperator, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator, FABL.productSingleCoordinateNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $B$ be a
finite orthonormal basis of functions on $\Omega$ whose constant vector is one of its
basis elements. For any natural number $n$, coordinate $i<n$, real $\rho$, and function
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, the product noise operator with parameter $\rho$ at coordinate
$i$ and parameter $1$ at every other coordinate equals the operator that leaves all
other coordinates unchanged and applies noise with parameter $\rho$ at coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Retention distribution for product noise]
\lean{FABL.productNoiseKeepPMF}
\label{FABL.productNoiseKeepPMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.nonnegativeCorrelationProbability, FABL.nonnegativeCorrelationProbability_le_one}
Let $\rho\in[0,1]$. The product-noise retention distribution is a probability mass
function on $\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ that assigns probability $p$ to retaining
a coordinate and probability $1-p$ to not retaining it, where $p$ is the
nonnegative-correlation probability associated with $\rho$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate noise probability mass function]
\lean{FABL.productCoordinateNoisePMF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b003}
\label{FABL.productCoordinateNoisePMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.productNoiseKeepPMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $x\in\Omega$, and
let $\rho\in[0,1]$. The coordinate noise probability mass function is the mixture that
retains $x$ with probability $\rho$ and otherwise draws a new value according to $\pi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product noise kernel]
\lean{FABL.productNoiseKernel}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b002
}
\label{FABL.productNoiseKernel}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.productCoordinateNoisePMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $\rho\in[0,1]$,
and let $x\in\Omega^n$. The product noise kernel at $x$ is the probability distribution
on $\Omega^n$ obtained by independently applying to each coordinate the noise rule that
retains its value with probability $\rho$ and otherwise draws from $\pi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Isotropic noise on a product basis function]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.pmfExpectation_productNoiseKernel_productFunction}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.pmfExpectation_productNoiseKernel_productFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.pmfExpectation_productCoordinateNoisePMF_basis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.multiIndexOrder, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_independentProductPMF_prod, FABL.productCoordinateNoisePMF, FABL.productNoiseKernel}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite Fourier basis on $\Omega$ indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$, with
distinguished constant basis index $0_B$. For $\rho\in[0,1]$, a point $x\in\Omega^n$,
and a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the expectation of the product basis function indexed
by $a$ under the product noise distribution at $x$ is $\rho^{d(a)}\prod_{i=1}^n
B_{a_i}(x_i)$, where $d(a)$ is the number of coordinates $i$ for which $a_i\ne 0_B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Product noise operator]
\lean{FABL.productNoiseOperator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b006
}
\label{FABL.productNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productNoiseKernel}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $\rho\in[0,1]$,
and let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The product noise operator sends $f$ to the
function whose value at $x\in\Omega^n$ is the expectation of $f$ under the product noise
kernel started at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of the product noise operator]
\lean{FABL.productNoiseOperator_add}
\label{FABL.productNoiseOperator_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.productNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $Ω$ be a finite set with probability mass function $π$,
and let $\rho\in[0,1]$. For any real-valued functions $f,g$ on $Ω^n$, applying the
product noise operator at parameter $\rho$ to $f+g$ gives the sum of its applications to
$f$ and to $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scalar linearity of product noise]
\lean{FABL.productNoiseOperator_smul}
\label{FABL.productNoiseOperator_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.productNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on it,
let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\rho\in[0,1]$. For every real scalar $c$ and
every real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, the product noise operator that
independently retains each coordinate with probability $\rho$ and otherwise
resamples from $\pi$ satisfies $T_\rho(cf)=cT_\rho f$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.productNoiseOperator}

  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the
constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, correlation parameter
$\rho\in[0,1]$, function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and input $x\in\Omega^n$, the
product noise operator applied to $f$ at $x$ equals $\sum_a
\rho^{|\operatorname{supp}(a)|}\widehat f(a)\,\phi_a(x)$, where the sum ranges over all
multi-indices, $\operatorname{supp}(a)$ is the set of coordinates where $a$ is not the
distinguished constant-basis index, $\widehat f(a)$ is the corresponding Fourier
coefficient, and $\phi_a$ is the corresponding product basis function.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient under product noise]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productNoiseOperator}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b007
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourier_expansion_unique, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productNoiseOperator_fourier_expansion, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexOrder, FABL.productNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a
finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by
$\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For
$\rho\in[0,1]$, let the product noise operator independently retain each input
coordinate with probability $\rho$ and otherwise resample it from $\pi$. For a function
$f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$ and a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient of
the noisy function at $a$ is $\rho^d$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$, where
$d$ is the number of coordinates where $a$ differs from the constant index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-adjointness of product noise]
\lean{FABL.productNoiseOperator_selfAdjoint}
\label{FABL.productNoiseOperator_selfAdjoint}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productNoiseOperator, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.plancherel, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInner, FABL.productNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function
on $\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of
the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ is given whose distinguished vector is the
constant-one function and which is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by
$\pi$. For any natural number $ n$, any $\rho\in[0,1]$, and any real-valued
functions $f,g$ on $\Omega^n$, the product noise operator that independently retains
each input coordinate with probability $\rho$ and otherwise resamples it from
$\pi$ is self-adjoint for the product inner product weighted by $\pi^n$:
$\langle f,T_\rho g\rangle=\langle T_\rho f,g\rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Product noise stability]
\lean{FABL.productNoiseStability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b006
}
\label{FABL.productNoiseStability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInner, FABL.productNoiseOperator}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
and let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$. For $0\leq\rho\leq1$, the product noise
stability of $f$ at parameter $\rho$ is the product-space inner product of $f$ with its
image under the product noise operator at parameter $\rho$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier formula for noise stability]

  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the
constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, correlation parameter
$\rho\in[0,1]$, and function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, the noise stability of $f$
equals $\sum_a \rho^{|\operatorname{supp}(a)|}\widehat f(a)^2$, summed over all
multi-indices $a$, where $\operatorname{supp}(a)$ consists of the coordinates at which
$a$ differs from the distinguished constant-basis index, and $\widehat f(a)$ is the
corresponding Fourier coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of spectral and probabilistic noise operators]
\lean{FABL.spectralProductNoiseOperator_eq_productNoiseOperator}
\label{FABL.spectralProductNoiseOperator_eq_productNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productNoiseOperator_fourier_expansion, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productNoiseOperator, FABL.spectralProductNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set with decidable equality. Suppose a real
orthonormal basis of functions on $\Omega$ is indexed by $\iota$, with one basis vector
equal to the constant-one function and with orthonormality taken in the inner product
weighted by $\pi$. For every natural number $n$, every correlation parameter
$\rho\in[0,1]$, and every real-valued function on $\Omega^n$, the operator defined by
weighting its product-basis Fourier coefficients by $\rho$ to the power of the number of
nonconstant coordinates equals the operator that, independently at each coordinate,
keeps the input with probability $\rho$ and otherwise resamples from $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\label{FABL.productStableInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.productNoiseStability}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and choose a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For
$0<\rho\leq1$, the stable influence of $f$ at coordinate $i$ is $\rho^{-1}$ times the
product noise stability at parameter $\rho$ of the coordinate Laplacian of $f$ at $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Total product stable influence]
\lean{FABL.productTotalStableInfluence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p057-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p215-b005
}
\label{FABL.productTotalStableInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productStableInfluence}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
and let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$. For $0<\rho\leq1$, the total stable influence of
$f$ is the sum, over all $n$ coordinates, of its stable influence at that coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Stable influence polynomial]
\lean{FABL.stableInfluencePolynomial}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p057-b002}
\label{FABL.stableInfluencePolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexOrder}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ for the $\pi$-weighted
inner product, with one basis vector equal to the constant-one function. Let its index
set be finite and nonempty, and let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, $i$ be a coordinate,
and $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$. The stable influence polynomial at $i$ is the sum over
multi-indices $a$ whose entry at $i$ is not the constant-vector index, of
$\rho^{|a|-1}\widehat f(a)^2$, where $|a|$ is the order of $a$ and $\widehat f(a)$ is
the Fourier coefficient of $f$ in the product basis.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positive order from a nonzero coordinate]
\lean{FABL.multiIndexOrder_pos_of_ne}
\label{FABL.multiIndexOrder_pos_of_ne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.multiIndexOrder, FABL.multiIndexSupport}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\iota$ be a type with decidable equality, choose
$z\in\iota$, and let $a:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\iota$. If some position $i$ satisfies
$a(i)\ne z$, then the number of positions $j$ with $a(j)\ne z$ is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of stable influence]
\lean{FABL.productStableInfluence_nonneg}
\label{FABL.productStableInfluence_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productStableInfluence_eq_polynomial, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productStableInfluence, FABL.stableInfluencePolynomial}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $\pi$. Suppose a
finite nonempty index set $\iota$ indexes a basis of the real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the
constant-one function as one basis vector. For every $\rho\in(0,1]$, every $n\ge 0$,
every function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and every coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the
stable influence of $f$ at coordinate $i$ with parameter $\rho$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Continuity of the stable influence polynomial]
\lean{FABL.continuous_stableInfluencePolynomial}
\label{FABL.continuous_stableInfluencePolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.stableInfluencePolynomial}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ and $I$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function
on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ indexed by
$I$, with one distinguished index whose basis function is constant $1$, and whose basis
functions are orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For any natural
number $n$, function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\bbr$, and coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
the stable influence polynomial in the real parameter $\rho$ is continuous.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero parameter influence polynomial]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.stableInfluencePolynomial_zero}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.stableInfluencePolynomial_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexOrder, FABL.multiIndexOrder_pos_of_ne, FABL.stableInfluencePolynomial}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose
constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted
inner product. For a positive integer $n$, any function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and
coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the stable influence polynomial at parameter zero
equals the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients over precisely those
multi-indices with exactly one nonzero coordinate and with that coordinate equal to $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Limit of the stable influence polynomial]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.tendsto_stableInfluencePolynomial_zero}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.tendsto_stableInfluencePolynomial_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.stableInfluencePolynomial_zero, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.continuous_stableInfluencePolynomial, FABL.multiIndexOrder, FABL.stableInfluencePolynomial}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$, with one basis vector equal to the constant-one function and with the basis
orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$. For every natural number $n$, every function
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and every coordinate $i$, the stable influence polynomial
at parameter $\rho$ tends, as $\rho\to0$, to the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients
over multi-indices of order one that are nonzero at coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p013-b007,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, suppose its variance under the product measure $\pi^n$ is at
most $1$. For each coordinate $i$, define its stable influence at parameter $1-\delta$
by summing $(1-\delta)^{|\{j:a_j\ne0\}|-1}\widehat f(a)^2$ over all product Fourier
indices $a$ with $a_i\ne0$, where $\widehat f(a)$ is the product Fourier coefficient. If
$0<\delta<1$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1$, then the number of coordinates whose stable
influence is at least $\varepsilon$ is at most $1/(\delta\varepsilon)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Counting coordinates with positive-degree influence]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.card_stableInfluencePolynomial_zero_ge_le}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.card_stableInfluencePolynomial_zero_ge_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.stableInfluencePolynomial_zero, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.variance_eq_sum_sq_fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.zeroMultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexOrder, FABL.multiIndexOrder_cast_eq_sum_indicator, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.productVariance, FABL.stableInfluencePolynomial}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, suppose its variance under the product measure $\pi^n$ is at
most $1$. Define the stable influence at parameter $0$ of coordinate $i$ as the sum of
$0^{|\{j:a_j\ne0\}|-1}\widehat f(a)^2$ over product Fourier indices with $a_i\ne0$, with
the exponent interpreted as natural-number subtraction. If $0<\varepsilon\le1$, then the
number of coordinates whose stable influence at parameter $0$ is at least $\varepsilon$
is at most $1/\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Sum of juntas of bounded width]
\lean{FABL.IsSumOfJuntasAtMost}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p036-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p215-b009
}
\label{FABL.IsSumOfJuntasAtMost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates, FABL.ProductL2}
Let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$. The function $f$ is a sum of
juntas of width at most $k$ if there is a function $g_J\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ for
each subset $J$ of the coordinates such that $g_J$ depends only on coordinates in $J$,
$g_J=0$ whenever $|J|>k$, and $f=\sum_J g_J$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Decomposition into coordinate juntas]
\lean{FABL.isSumOfJuntasAtMost_dimension}
\label{FABL.isSumOfJuntasAtMost_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates, FABL.IsSumOfJuntasAtMost, FABL.ProductL2}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be any type, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f$ be a real-valued
function on $\Omega^n$. Then $f$ can be written as a sum indexed by subsets
$J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, where each summand depends only on the coordinates in its
indexing set $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Product degree]
\lean{FABL.productDegree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p036-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p215-b009
}
\label{FABL.productDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.isSumOfJuntasAtMost_dimension}
Let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The product degree of $f$ is the least natural
number $k$ for which $f$ is a sum of juntas each depending on at most $k$ coordinates.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zero}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p211-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p211-b005}
\proofstep
  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite Fourier basis on $(\Omega,\pi)$ indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$.
For a finite set $\kappa$, a natural number $n$, a family of real-valued functions $f_j$
on $\Omega^n$ indexed by $j\in\kappa$, and a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier
coefficient of their pointwise sum is the sum of their Fourier coefficients:
$\widehat{\sum_{j\in\kappa} f_j}(a)=\sum_{j\in\kappa}\widehat{f_j}(a)$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite Fourier basis on $\Omega$ indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$, with
distinguished constant basis index $0_B$. For every multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the
product basis function indexed by $a$ depends only on the coordinates $i$ for which
$a_i\ne 0_B$; that is, its values agree at any two points of $\Omega^n$ that agree on
all those coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fourier component with prescribed support]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierComponentAtSupport}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p216-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p217-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p219-b003
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierComponentAtSupport}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexSupport}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ for the $\pi$-weighted
inner product, with one basis vector equal to the constant-one function. Let its index
set be finite and nonempty, let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and let $J$ be a subset
of the coordinates. The Fourier component of $f$ with support exactly $J$ is the sum,
over multi-indices whose support is $J$, of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ times the
corresponding product basis function.
\end{definition}

\proofstep
  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis indexed by a finite nonempty set
$\iota$. For every integer $n\geq 0$, every function $f\colon \Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$,
and every set of coordinates $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the sum of the Fourier terms
indexed by multi-indices whose support is exactly $J$ depends only on the coordinates in
$J$: whenever $x,y\in\Omega^n$ agree on all coordinates in $J$, this sum has the same
value at $x$ and $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficient of a fixed support component]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_fourierComponentAtSupport}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_fourierComponentAtSupport}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_ite, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_productFunction, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_smul, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_sum, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zero, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierComponentAtSupport, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexSupport}
\difficulty{5}
Let $Ω$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $π$, and let $ι$ be a finite
nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions on $Ω$ that is
orthonormal for the $π$-weighted inner product and has a distinguished index $0_B$ whose
basis function is constantly one. For every $n\ge 0$, function $f:Ω^n\to\mathbb R$,
coordinate set $J$, and multi-index $a\inι^n$, the Fourier coefficient at $a$ of the
component of $f$ consisting of terms whose nonconstant coordinates are exactly $J$
equals the coefficient of $f$ at $a$ when the nonconstant-coordinate set of $a$ is $J$,
and equals zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.signMultiIndex_order}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p013-b007,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $(b_j)_{j\in\iota}$ is a basis of the
real-valued functions on $\Omega$, with $b_{j_0}$ the constant-one function for some
$j_0\in\iota$, and with $mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}[b_j(x)b_k(x)]$ equal to $1$ when $j=k$ and
$0$ otherwise. For every natural number $n$ and every real-valued function $f$ on
$n$-tuples from $\Omega$, the sum, over all subsets $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, of the
Fourier components of $f$ whose multi-indices differ from $j_0$ exactly on $J$ equals
$f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing Fourier component at fixed support]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierComponentAtSupport_eq_zero}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierComponentAtSupport_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierComponentAtSupport, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexSupport}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis on $\Omega$ indexed by a finite nonempty
set $\iota$. For an integer $n\ge 0$, let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$ and
let $J$ be a set of coordinates in $\mathrm{Fin}\ n$. If every multi-index whose support
is exactly $J$ has Fourier coefficient of $f$ equal to zero, then the Fourier component
of $f$ at support $J$ is the zero function.
\end{theorem}
